analysis:
Examined the doc-only changes to docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (GLM reasoning-control and JSON/tool-choice rows, which now describe output validation rather than refusals) and the fixtures README. These add no wire field or trust grant. Lines 1147-1155 state that the model is selected from the loaded model_type, not from caller input. They also state that non-conforming forced-tool or JSON output returns a 422 with nothing exposed, and that reserved schema metadata is rejected. These statements are consistent with T-056 (no overclaim) and the fail-closed posture. The doc itself says the fixtures do not qualify any of these modes. One open integration question: the described post-validation behavior lives in provider source that is not in the supplied units, so I could not verify it.

The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer moved from 7bed821 to baca4ac. Its contents are not supplied, so the effect on inference and KV-cache behavior (TB-007, T-028, T-041) cannot be assessed. Reviewers should check that submodule diff.

The new file provider-swift/.../Diagnostics/GLM5NextWiredLimit.swift is advice-only. It reads sysctl values (iogpu.wired_limit_mb and the user wire limits) and Metal's recommended working set, and returns text with sysctl commands and a LaunchDaemon plist for the operator to run manually. Nothing in the file executes commands, writes a plist, or escalates privilege. The plist and sysctl strings are built from constants and computed integers, not from untrusted input, so there is no injection path. The notice is documented to carry no request or model content. The file is also not wired into admission or capacity. The unreviewed callers (a doctor command and error handling) are not supplied. They should be checked to confirm they never auto-install the daemon and never log error text containing prompts. The isMetalOutOfMemory error matching is string-based and is a diagnostic only. No regression was identified in the supplied units.
